And watch the stars fill up the sky
He never talked a whole lot then
But somehow always knew just when

To let the silence have its say
And leave the rest for another day

I thought you were named after me

Christmas came the way it should
With wrapping paper, food, and wood
And there you'd sit beside the tree
The same chair every year I'd see

Not loud enough to fill a room
Yet somehow chased away the gloom
The kind of man who didn't need
To prove a single thing he'd be

Just steady as the winter snow
And always there when we would go

I thought you were named after me

The years rolled on the way they do
School and work and growing too
The things that seemed so far away
Became the things that filled my days

Years have a way of changing things
The truth arrives on quiet wings
Not through words or grand displays
But through countless ordinary days

The kind you never think about
Until you realize your time runs out

I thought you were named after me

The older photos lost their shade
The campfire light began to fade
The shooting trips, the fishing line
The countless moments lost to time

And looking back it seems to me
That child believed so earnestly
somewhere through the passing years
The joke became a little clear

We might have shared the same name
But that was never what remained

I thought you were named after me

Now when I sit by evening fires
Or watch the smoke from burning tires
I find myself in quiet thought
Of all the things those years had taught

Not through words or grand displays
But through countless ordinary days
And if there's one thing time has shown
how much he influenced how I've grown

Funny how life can sometimes be
I thought you were named after me

title: Nana's Prayers
lyrics:
The house was loud, the nights were long
Some days it felt like all was wrong
I learned too young to hide the hurt
And wear a smile when things got worse

The walls could shake, the tempers flare
Some wounds were more than I could bear
I didn't know what else to do
But Nana always seemed to

Nana's prayers got me through
When life was truly blue

The years rolled on, I lost my way
Made choices I still curse today
The papers talked, the rumors spread
And painted futures filled with dread

They swore I'd never rise again
That one mistake would be the end
I heard those words and thought them true
But Nana never seemed to

Nana's prayers got me through
When my penance was due

The voices came in different forms
Some whispered soft, some came as storms
They spoke of fear, they spoke of shame
And knew exactly where to aim

She'd tell me not to give them room
The darkest thoughts lead to doom
When I could barely see it through
Nana always seemed to

Nana's prayers got me through
When I could only trust few

The doctors spoke in careful tones
pain that brought only groan
A chest cut open, scars to keep
And fears that followed into sleep

Then years would bring another pain
A different kind, a deeper strain
The day my stepson went away
And every answer seemed delayed

I wasn't sure what still remained
Or if my life was to be drained
When every prayer felt hard to do
Still Nana always seemed to

Nana's prayers got me through
When it was time I grew
More than I ever knew

The years moved on the way they do
And somehow all those prayers pulled through
Not every wound was washed away
Not every night gave way to day

But every storm that came for me
Found someone on her knees between
The weight I carried and the fall
She stood there through it all

Then one day roles began to change
The strong grew tired, life rearranged
Machines and monitors filled the room
And doctors spoke of coming doom

For years she'd bowed her head for me
Through every storm I couldn't see
The woman who had carried mine
Now needed someone by her side

I folded hands beside my bed
And spoke the words she'd always said
I didn't know what heaven knew
But finally I knew what to do

Then I prayed for Nana too

title: Never Got to Know You
lyrics:
I know your face from years gone by
A few old stories passed in time
The kind of things that families share
When someone isn't sitting there

Different towns and different years
Kept us apart more than they appeared
By eighteen all I really knew
Was that somewhere the world held you

Then one June morning changed the air
And left a silence sitting there

I never got to know you

They spoke of the way you would grin
The friends you made,  trouble you'd been in
The jokes you'd tell, the things you'd say
Small pieces carried far away

I listened close to every word
Trying to make the picture  heard
But every story left me with
Another piece I somehow missed

The more I gathered, strange but true
The more I knew I never knew you

I never got to know you

A little girl not one year old
Too young to keep what she'd been told
Too young to hear your voice and laugh
Or build a single memory on your behalf

She'll never know the things you liked
Or hear your side of any fight
She'll only know what others knew
And try to build a version of you

And every time that thought comes through
It feels familiar somehow too

She never got to know you

One faded shirt inside a box
Has made each move from stop to stop
Across the country, back again
It somehow follows where I've been

A mark in ink upon my skin
The only thing that time can't thin
Not proof of moments that we shared
Just proof I wish they'd once been there

The years move on the way they do
Yet some things never quite pass through

I never got to know you

Sometimes I wonder who you'd see
If you could sit and talk with me
Would we get along, disagree
Or laugh at things nobody can see

Would you be proud of where I've been
The fights I've lost, the fights I'd win
The answers faded years ago
Along with things I'll never know

Some questions time won't answer to
No matter how long you pursue

I never got to know you

The older that I come to be
The more this truth returns to me
Not every loss is memory
Some losses live in treachery

The brother, father, years denied
By distance, fate, and passing time
Two different lives still owed a due
The same thing taken from us two

For all the years that came and went
For all the wondering we've spent

We never got to know you
We never got to know you

title: Not Through Yet
lyrics:
I watched you sleeping in your bed
And worried what lay just ahead
The world felt bigger than my sight
And darker than the coming night

I tried to be what you deserved
A steady hand, a guiding word
The road was long, the years unsure

Of things I do not wish to know
A life preserved, a soul retained
A mortal from his end restrained

Withheld.
That is the word he said.
Withheld.
But withheld from what?

The answer slowly fills my head
And suddenly I know the dread
No sickness waits to claim my breath
No age will lead me into death

"No."

The word escapes before I know
I shake my head and whisper, "No."
"There has to be an end someday.
All living things must pass away."

He tells me I will never age
As though I've slipped beyond a cage
No failing heart, no final breath
My life withheld from even Death

I claw my fingers through my hair
I gasp and struggle for the air
"You call this life? You call this grace?
Then put me back the right place!"

But Death just stands and watches me
As calm as endless night can be
I scream until my throat is sore
"Make me the man I was before!"

There is no spell he can reverse.
No simple end to break this curse.
The thing he made will now remain
Untouched by age, disease or pain

I look upon my trembling hand
And finally begin to understand
This flesh will never turn to dust
These bones will never break from rust

A hundred years.

A thousand more.

Ten thousand waiting at my door.

I try to count how long I'll stay
But numbers simply fall away
For every year that I survive
Another waits while I'm alive

There is no number large enough
No final page, no final breath
No distant shore that waits for me
No end to what I now must be

Forever.

I had spoken it before.
A foolish word and nothing more.
A promise lovers liked to say
For things they knew would fade away

Forever never frightened me
When it was something none could see
When every man who spoke its name
Would one day die all the same

But I will know what others won't.
I will endure when others don't.
The sun may rise, the mountains fall

And I may live beyond them all.
No.
No, I don't want this.
Take it back.
Please.
I was a man.
Let me remain one.

Let me grow old.
Let my hands shake.
Let my eyes fail.
Let my body break.

Give me the years that I was owed
And let me walk the mortal road
Give me a grave, give me an end
Let death still greet me as a friend

I do not want eternity
I do not want what's been given me
If every ending passes by
What will remain when I sigh.

title: All But I
lyrics:
I watched the first of kingdoms rise
With banners bright beneath the skies
They swore their walls would never fall
I watched the ivy claim them all

Their children built upon the stone
And claimed the age as their own
They spoke of kings both fierce and wise
I watched all of their demise

They bent the knee and called me lord
Raised gilded temples and sang chords
They prayed my favor as I was above
And slew their sons as signs of love

I warned them all what time would bring
That crowns mean little to a king
Whose eyes have watched the seasons turn
And seen a thousand cities burn

Empires rise and empires fall
The earth remembers none at all
The tallest towers scrape the sky
Then crumble just as grass will die

The wisest men and strongest hands
Still build their castles out of sand
And every age that thinks it stays
Becomes a tale of bygone days

At last I watched the old world end
I said it so but they couldn't comprehend
roads were lost, books are gone
I stand alone at the dawn

Time took that they thought would stay
Their monuments returned to clay
And all the things they swore would last
Were swallowed by the distant past

I stood where mighty kingdoms stood
Their marble halls consumed by wood
And when the final fire grew dim
The world forgot that time is Grimm

So heed these words while yet you may
The mountains too shall fade away
For all beneath the endless sky
Must yield to time and learn to die

This is true for all but I

title: Changeling
lyrics:
I came into this world half-broke
A sickly little pathetic joke.
They wrapped me up and sent me home...
Though something always felt unknown.
I learned the rules the humans made,
Then somehow failed them anyway.
They'd laugh and say, "You're kinda strange."
I figured I was built that way.
I missed the cues, misunderstood,
Did what they said a person should.
But every time I played the part...
The script and I would drift apart.
So maybe I'm a changeling,
Left where human children sleep.
Maybe someone crossed the veil...
And somehow they forgot to switch me.
Maybe somewhere past the trees,
There's a place that makes more sense to me.
Where no one thinks I'm strange at all...
They're just surprised I grew this tall.
Then daylight joined the evidence.
A few short minutes? Consequence.
The sun comes out, I stay inside...
Apparently I cannot Thrive...
I've always loved the later hours,
Midnight streets and sleeping flowers.
The world gets quiet after three...
And finally feels awake to me.
Still, none of that means anything.
Some people simply hate the spring.
Some burn too fast beneath the sun...
Then I discovered Iron.
...
Well, fuck.
Because iron doesn't like me much.
My skin objects to every touch.
Even surgical steel can leave
A lovely little mark on me.
Now I'm not saying that's a sign.
I'm only saying...
It's a sign.
So maybe I'm a changeling,
And someone botched the trade.
Left me sleeping in a crib...
Then wandered off and got waylaid.
Maybe I was meant for somewhere
Moonlight doesn't hurt my eyes.
Where iron stays outside the door...
And no one asks why I'm awake at five.
Perhaps beyond the hawthorn hedge,
Past mortal map and woodland edge,
Some court still keeps an empty chair
And wonders how I'm doing here.
Perhaps I should be keeping court,
Or making mischief for the sport.
Trading riddles, names, and lies—
No.
Not lies.
Carefully constructed technical truths.

Forsooth! What fool hath left me here
'Mong fluorescent lights and fiscal years?
When yonder moon through thicket gleams,
I should be trafficking in dreams!
With merry measure, moonlit leisure,
pilfered treasure, debts of pleasure;
word for word and boon for boon,
binding bargains beneath the moon.
Hither, thither, round the ring,
mind thy manners when bells sing;
name me not and thank me never,
mind thy tongue and mind the weather.
By briar, bower, bell and bone,
by paths that shift when walked alone,
by "thee" and "thine" and "hast thou brought
the bloody thing for which I sought?"
I'd mince my meaning, twist the telling,
weave three truths through every spelling;
rhyme the reason, season, treason,
steal thy name for no good reason—
Dance till dawn through dew and thyme,
lose a decade, swear it's nine;
trade a favor, steal a rhyme,
return thee home...
three centuries behind.
...
See?
I'm weirdly good at this.
So maybe I'm a changeling.
At this point, who can say?
I've survived the human world this long...
Which feels impressive anyway.
Maybe somewhere through the trees
My people wonder where I've been.
Some ancient thing looks toward the veil
And mutters, "He survived again?"
I know it's only make-believe.
A running joke I've learned to keep.
But some nights underneath the moon...
It doesn't sound so strange to me.
Maybe I'm not made all wrong.
Maybe I've been misplaced all along.
Maybe somewhere waits a land
Where all my edges understand.
every time I played the part...
The script and I drift apart.
So I think I'm a changeling,
Left where human children sleep.
Back then someone crossed the veil...
And somehow they forgot about me.
somewhere past the trees,
There's a place that makes more sense to me.
Where no one thinks I'm strange at all...
They're just surprised I have no thrall
And if someday the veil grows thin,
And something whispers, "Come on in..."
I'll leave one note beside my bed:
"Went home.
Back in ten."

title: Mind Thy Tongue
lyrics:
Oh, mortal darling.
That was adorable.
Now watch this.

Thou cam’st to the hedge with a rhyme newly wrought,
Three briars, two bargains, one secondhand thought;
With moonlight in pockets and pride in thy pen,
Then signed thy farewell with a vague “Back in ten.”

“Word for word and boon for boon?”

Sweetling, thou hast spoken too soon.
A syllable sells what a sentence never tells;
A whisper may witness, a question may claim,
And courtesy collects what no answer would name.

For bargains hide braided in breath and behavior,
In favors that flavor the fee of the fae;
A curtsy may purchase, a compliment cost,
And “take what thou needest” leaves ownership lost.

Mind promise from premise, permission from plea,
The gift from the giving, the giver from thee;
Mind may against might, shall against should—
One carefully crooked conjunction draws blood.

Thou boastest of taking a name?
How quaint.

A name is a knocker, a handle, a hinge;
I’d rather take the why thou wouldst answer or flinch.
Keep every last letter, each title and claim—
I’ll leave thee forgetting why thou answerest thy name.

Keep pace, little stray; lend a rhyme if thou can,
And follow my measure wherever it ran.

By willow-writ warrants and foxglove decrees,
By moth-eaten monarchs who mortgage the breeze,
By paths taking payment in footprints and breath,
By doors saying “welcome” while meaning “enter debt.”

Thou misplaced a decade and called it a feat?
Ten years in a thicket? How charmingly neat.
I swallowed a Sunday, split spring into seven,
Then pawned one blue Tuesday for half of heaven.

I folded a fortnight through four generations,
Made midnights miss mornings in six separate nations;
Lent August to autumn, gave winter to June,
Then charged them both interest in splinters of moon.

A bargain needs neither thy blood nor thy pen;
Just finish the thought, I’ll leave at—


Which brings us, dear wanderer...
“Back in ten?”
Ten what?

Ten heartbeats?
Ten tollings of bells?
Ten winters? Ten weddings? Ten empires fell?

Darling.
Specify.
Now, where was I?

Aye, truth may be twisted while never untrue,
And every fair statement may hide something due;
The trick isn’t lying—how terribly crude—
It’s serving the truth with the context removed.

Say “freely,” say “fairly,” say “favor,” say “friend,”
Say “only until,” but say nothing of when;
Say “take what thou wishest,” then smile as they choose,
For wanting and having make a marvelous noose.

A clause may grow claws; a fine may mean fair,
Then fine thee one fortune for touching my hair.
A sentence may sentence; a term may be time;
A present, a presence, a gift, or a crime.

I’ll puncture with punctuation, comma thee still,
Put periods where thou hadst promised “until”;
Make colons collect and apostrophes own,
Then bracket thy body and parenthesize bone.

Briar becomes buyer; the bower, borrower;
Morrow grows mourner and sorrow, sorcerer.
Favor turns flavor, then fee, then forfeiture;
Interest blossoms, growing fetters from favors.

Clauses grow talons, conditions grow teeth,
Courtesy curtsies while contracts coil beneath;
Loopholes loop lightly through lavender law,
And technical truth keeps a knife at your jaw.

Trip over trochees and tumble through trimeter;
Meddle with meter till meter grows meaner;
Rhyme within rhyme within reasonless reason;
Squeeze in a season for meaningless treason.

Mark me, unmake me, mistake and remake me;
Name me, disclaim me, then blame what thou gav’st me.
Bedevil the bevel, bewilder the wise,
Hide riddles in middles and middles in—

Lies?
No.
We covered this.
Do pay attention.

By thorn-thrum and thunder, by bell-blood and bloom,
By bramble-born brides bearing bargains to doom;
By never, nevertheless, neither nor naught,
By aught that was offered and ought that was bought;

By vellum and venom, by covenant ink,
By all thou hast uttered before thou couldst think;
By “freely,” by “fairly,” by “only,” by “friend”—

Thou granted me something.
Didst notice?
No?

Thou gavest it the moment
Thou didst finish my line.
Relax.
I took only a rhyme.

And truthfully, strayling, thy tongue carries wit;
Thy ear catches cadence, thy instincts half-fit.
There’s art in thy mischief and nerve in thy need—

But talent is tinder.
Not mastery.
Not deed.

So come to the hawthorn when moonlight wears thin.
Bring neither cold iron nor certainty in.
Bring riddles with fractures and questions unwise,
Ten versions of truth and eleven replies.

We’ll teach thee the measure, the menace, the mien,
The courtesy cruel and the cruelty clean;
How promises prosper, how loopholes are spun,
How bargains lie ended—
Yet never are done.

Thou may yet make a menace.
Thou may yet make a name.
Thou may yet learn the rules
Of our ridiculous game.

But next time thou swaggerest, proud of thy pen,
And leavest a note saying—
“Back in ten.”

One rhyme makes no master.
One trick no sage.
The hedge has humbled monarch and mage.
Thou mayst have the tongue and talent to turn—
But pride is the lesson thou hast yet to learn.

title: A Rhyme Short
lyrics:
Oh, very impressive.

Really.

Weaponized grammar.
Contract law with flowers.
Terrifying.

But if we're keeping score,
I think I deserve some credit.

I came to thy hedge with no map and no guide,
No whispering court with its rules at my side.
No tutor to teach me what courtesy costs,
Which gifts become fetters, which favors get lost.

Yet I found iron and favors and names,
The weight of a word and the shape of your games.
I learned technical truth without knowing you lived—
That what isn't spoken may matter as much as what's giv'n.

So yes, thou art clever.
Yes, thou art old.
And apparently every sentence has seventeen folds.

But centuries sharpen what instinct began,
And I've had a few decades—

You're grading a man
Who learned from old stories, from meter and plays,
Then wandered your hedge and got most of the ways.

I mistook a few rules.
I'll happily grant it.
But frankly, considering the obvious disadvantage—

I think I did well.

You called me talented.
I heard that part.
Buried beneath all the linguistic art.
"Thy tongue carries wit." Those words were thine,
So let me demonstrate rather than whine.

A promise needs premise, a premise precision;
Permission unbounded invites an incision.
A gift without limits leaves ownership blurred,
And intent means nothing beside the given word.

"Freely" means freely—but freely to what?
"Only" means little till limits are cut.
A favor gains interest, a courtesy debt,
And the safest agreement is one not made yet.

See?

I was listening.

A clause may have claws—
Fine, clever, well played—
But claws can be counted once properly displayed.
Define every term and delineate scope,
And even thy labyrinth leaves me a rope.

Forsooth, fair lady, perhaps thou shouldst—

...

No.

I'm not doing that.

You win the "thou" thing.

But language is language.
Your rules aren't divine.
If meaning has structure, that structure has lines.
And lines can be studied, exceptions discerned,
A pattern once witnessed's a pattern half-learned.

You had centuries sharpening every phrase.
I've had sleepless nights and fluorescent days,
A stack of old plays and too much free time,
And still taught myself how to weaponize rhyme.

So give me a year and I'll answer thy best.
Give me a decade, I'll master the—

...

...

Hm.

That's odd.

I know that word.

Obviously I know that word.

The meter wants it.
The sentence is set.
The rhyme should be—

...

No.

Not "test."

That isn't—

Wait.

...

"Lend a rhyme if thou can."

Oh.

You said—

"I took only a rhyme."

...

You took **that** rhyme.

Not my rhyming.

Not my talent.

One rhyme.

And you knew exactly which one I'd need.

...

You absolute—

No.

No, that's good.

That's *really* good.

You told me what you'd taken.
Every word was true.
I understood the sentence—

I misunderstood **you**.

So that's the difference.

I know the words.
You know where they lead.
I recognize bargains.
You recognize need.

I can follow the branches once shown where they run.
You see the whole tree while the seed's still begun.

...

Fine.

You win.

For now.

Don't look so pleased.

You're better than me.

There.
Enjoy it.

And I could spend another verse defending my pride,
Or admit there's an obvious lesson implied:

If someone is better
at something I love,
I'd rather learn from them
than pretend I'm enough.

So—

Teach me.

...

Oh, fuck me.

No.

Absolutely not.

I **request** instruction,
shouldst thou freely agree,
in the customs and language
employed by the Thee;

No ownership granted of body or name,
No unspecified favor, no undefined claim,
No payment implied beyond terms we both state,
No debt retroactive to choosing my fate.

No shadow, no memory, no year of my life,
No metaphorical "hand," no conveniently "wife,"
No firstborn—

Don't have one.

And nothing unspoken shall constitute price.

...

Better?

Good.

Then teach me thy measure.
I'll answer in mine.
Teach me the difference
'tween wording and sign.

Show me the loopholes,
the courtesy's teeth,
The promise above
and the bargain beneath.

I won't promise humility.
Let's not pretend.

But I'll come to the hawthorn
and learn where words bend.

No iron.
No certainty.
Questions in ten—

...

Actually—

Let's not use numbers
until you explain those again.

And someday, when mastery catches my pen,
I'll know exactly what I mean
when I write—

"Back in ten."

title: Little Stray
lyrics:
Well that was disappointing
I fashioned six answers and polished each snare
Prepared for objection, denial, despair
Expected these snarlings that somehow I cheated
And then little stray, that was simply conceited
No wounded objection, no challenge, no plea
No clever construction assigning fault to me
No mortal insistence that losing the game
Must surely imply that the rules are the blame
Really?
I thought thee more stubborn
I thought thee more proud
I pictured thy protest both lengthy and loud
Instead thou discovered the place thou wert wrong
Considered the lesson, then carried along
How very peculiar
For mortals love pride with astonishing zeal
They'll fracture the mirror before they will kneel
They'll cherish an error, defend it for years
Then call themselves victors when truth disappears
Yet thou wert defeated, reviewed the event
Then asked how the trick worked and where the rhyme went
I thought pride thy weakness
It seems I mistook
The flourish for foundation
The cover for book
Thou certainly swagger, thou certainly preen
Thou findest thy cleverness terribly keen
But place reputation against something new
And pride, without ceremony
Loses To you
Interesting
Now, By request
No ownership granted of body or name
No unspecification favour, no undefined claim
No payment implied beyond terms we both state
No debt retroactive to choosing my fate
A promising effort
Thou guarded thy shadow, thy memory, thy life
Thy future, thy firstborn, thy hypothetical wife
Thou barred implication and payment inferred
Then trusted thy safety as a safety
To one little word
Expressly
By whom? By thee, or by me?
By witness or custom, by gesture decree
To silence express when convention says yes
Just conduct convey what thy tongue won't confess

There is the face I had hoped I would see, not anger
Calculation
Much better
Precision, dear straying, is not speaking long
It is knowing precisely where meaning goes wrong
A fortress of clauses may still leave a door
If one undefined word undermines the floor, but
For thy first construction
It will serve
Thou asked for instruction
Should I freely agree?
I do
That expression again
What is the price?
None
No favor concealed and no future demand
No leaning on thy shadow, thy voice, or thy hand
No service unspoken, no payment deferred
I teach thee because
I desire it
My word
Still searching for loopholes
Good
I should have been wounded had one song cured thee
Come then, bring Shakespeare thy questions, thy nerve
Bring every objection thy wit can preserve
Bring riddles half-broken and arguments bent
And learn why the wording outlives the intent
First premise and promise, permission and scope
How certainty strangles and vagueness makes rope
Then courtesy favors, acceptance, and debts
Then names
No, not yet
Thou hast barely learned what a pronoun can cost thee
Do not pout
There is something, however,
I wish understood
I expected thy talent
I knew it was good
Thy ear catches cadence
Thy tongue carries wit
Thy instinct finds pathways
Where mortals misstep
But talent was never what altered my view
It was what thou didst when I proved better than you
No tantrum, no fiction, no comforting lie
No desperate reason why loss shouldn't apply
Thou looked at a master, acknowledged the gap
Then asked for a lesson to narrow it back
Mortals are strange
But thou art strange
Even for them
So yes, I shall teach thee
I will not make error more pleasant to hear
I will not make difficult lessons less clear
I will not call failure a victory won
When there are still seventeen ways it goes wrong
Thou asked for the measure, the menace, the craft
Then learn when I teach thee, and someday perhaps
When thou swaggerest in, I'll sharpen nine answers and wonder which wins
Until then, little stray
Bring thy troublesome pen
And this time, when leaving,
Specify
Ten

title: Precisely
lyrics:

If all thou canst do is take language apart.

A master does more than discover the snare;

[MALE VOCAL ]

stands outside thy door.

[FEMALE VOCAL]

[MALE VOCAL]
“My fire burns warmly; the night's getting cold.

[MALE VOCAL ]
[MALE VOCAL ]

“Come out of the cold, should the threshold entice.
